taylor_tail: after choosing K so the absolute-term ratio at K is at most r<1, the omitted absolute tail is bounded by term_K/(1-r); use the interval upper endpoint to choose r
asymptotic_tail: repeated integration by parts gives R_K the next alternating sign and absolute value at most (2K-1)!!/(2x^2)^K
hybrid: use Taylor with absolute-tail enclosure on bounded small/middle x and the integration-by-parts enclosure on large x
directed_rounding: all rational polynomial terms are exact; sqrt(pi), exp(-x^2), interval powers, and final arithmetic still require outward-rounded elementary enclosures
acceptance_test: Implement directed enclosures for pi, square root, and exponential, apply the hybrid erfc bounds to every accelerated-gamma term, sum with outward rounding, and propagate to the four D2 samples.
